slot.brief: Figure shows an alcohol and a target ether; choose the best halide–alkoxide combination and conditions for a high-yield Williamson synthesis.

stem: For the conversion shown in the figure, which reagent pair and conditions are best for a high-yield Williamson synthesis?
options: $\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ and sodium ethoxide in dry acetone
tert-Butyl bromide and sodium methoxide in dry acetone
$\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ and sodium tert-butoxide in dry acetone
Ethyl bromide and sodium tert-butoxide in dry acetone

verdicts.working: The product is methyl tert-butyl ether. Williamson synthesis forms it by SN2 attack of tert-butoxide on methyl bromide; tertiary halides favor elimination instead.

working:
The target ether has a tert-butyl group and a methyl group bonded to oxygen.
Use the bulky tert-butoxide as the alkoxide and methyl bromide as the primary halide.
$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{CO}^- + \text{CH}_3\text{Br}\rightarrow \text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COCH}_3$

Independent check: The product is methyl tert-butyl ether. Williamson synthesis forms it by SN2 attack of tert-butoxide on methyl bromide; tertiary halides favor elimination instead.
solution:
Williamson synthesis proceeds by an $S_N2$ reaction; methyl bromide is ideal, while tert-butoxide supplies the bulky alkoxide.
$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{CO}^- + \text{CH}_3\text{Br} \longrightarrow \text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COCH}_3$$
Thus, methyl tert-butyl ether is obtained in high yield using methyl bromide and sodium tert-butoxide in dry acetone.
